upsert.title: ePUSH precision-medicine treatment study for canine splenic hemangiosarcoma
upsert.status: Open — current Ethos Discovery study page
upsert.contacts: Enrollment/request-information form on the official Ethos Discovery study page; participating hospitals listed there
upsert.funding: $1,000 toward splenectomy; confirmed non-metastatic HSA patients continuing to treatment phase receive fully funded study treatment; up to $3,000 toward treatment of study-related adverse effects.
upsert.notes: Umbrella precision-medicine program. Initial enrollment occurs around splenectomy for a ruptured splenic tumor; dogs confirmed with HSA and no metastasis can proceed to a treatment phase using therapies matched to molecular subtype. Treat as one multicenter protocol, not one record per participating specialty hospital.

upsert.title: Combination immunotherapy after surgery for canine high-grade glioma / glioblastoma
upsert.status: Actively recruiting — current PRECINCT glioblastoma clinical-trials page
upsert.funding: Confirm current study-covered and owner-paid costs with the investigator.
upsert.notes: PRECINCT describes an interventional therapeutic study evaluating postoperative combination immunotherapy strategies, including autologous tumor-lysate vaccination plus immune modulation/checkpoint blockade and an immune-based gene-therapy strategy. Keep as the canonical PRECINCT/UMN protocol rather than duplicating recruitment/news pages.

upsert.title: Oncolytic virus IL-12 immunotherapy after surgery for canine malignant glioma
upsert.status: Actively recruiting — current PRECINCT glioblastoma clinical-trials page
upsert.contacts: Regional sites listed by PRECINCT: Auburn University, University of Georgia, Mississippi State University, Purdue University and Tuskegee University; UAB coordinating contact also listed on primary page.
upsert.funding: Confirm current study-covered and owner-paid costs with the regional study site.
upsert.notes: Phase I open-label dose-escalation study. Surgical resection is followed by an oncolytic virus engineered to express IL-12; after a tolerable dose is established the therapy is combined with checkpoint inhibition. One multicenter protocol record covers all participating sites.
